Thanks Maria — we see the same spikes in our hosted API dashboards matching your request ids. Im looping in our runtime and SRE leads to triage. Immediate plan: 

- Confirmed: p95/p99 regressions correlate strongly with requests >8k tokens.
- Short-term mitigations we can enact within the hour: route long-context requests to a dedicated long-window pool (fallback model with pinned KV cache), throttle large-request concurrency per-tenant, and temporarily raise HTTP timeouts for your tenant to avoid user-facing 504s while we investigate.
- Investigation items: live traces and kernel metrics to check KV cache eviction and batching behavior, request-level batching profiles for large sequences.

Please confirm if you approve temporary routing/throttling (well keep you updated once changes are applied). We will avoid any model changes that could alter outputs without your signoff.

On Fri, Apr 2, 2027 at 08:30, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai wrote:
> Immediate plan: route long-context requests to a dedicated long-window pool (fallback model with pinned KV cache), throttle large-request concurrency per-tenant, and temporarily raise HTTP timeouts

Quick technical notes from runtime: were observing severe KV-cache churn when sequence lengths exceed ~8k tokens in conjunction with our dynamic batching. The effect: 1) serialization on the main serving thread while KV buffers are being swapped, and 2) batches with a single long sequence increase end-to-end GPU kernel time dramatically, raising p99 across the worker. A few concrete options: 

Short-term (fast, low-risk):
- Reduce dynamic batch window for sequences >8k to avoid mixing long and short sequences.
- Pin the tenants cache entries for 2 hours to reduce eviction churn.
- Force long-context requests onto the long-window fleet (separate workers configured for 32k).

Medium-term (next 48-72h):
- Deploy kernel-level micro-optimizations we prepared (improved KV eviction heuristics + smaller attention kernel for >16k). Patch ready as runtime_patch.diff.
- Add a per-tenant batching policy to avoid cross-tenant tail amplification.

I can push the short-term config changes now if customer approves. Attaching runtime_patch.diff for the follow-on deployment (non-disruptive tests completed in staging).

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
